scope: Shared bounded RustFS process-pause scheduling and independent acknowledgement-window evidence for Raft, Fleet and bucket benchmark adapters. Harness implementation only; zero new physical runs.
implementation: Both launchers accept s3-outage and healthy controls with a checked object-store fault profile; unsupported capabilities, missing profiles and invalid bounds refuse before workload resources.

A joined fault owner uses the existing persistent Docker API adapter to bind exact name, ownership and immutable ID. Lost pause/resume replies are inspected. Failed or cancelled attempts retain their evidence and cannot qualify.

Every scheduled window requires a fresh successful command dispatched after the observed hold and before release starts. The journal records the post-fsync dispatch timestamp; generator admission, scheduled arrival and journal delay cannot substitute for that observation.
S3 and bucket policies refuse acknowledgements during the observed hold. Quorum and Fleet may acknowledge using their distinct contracts; no per-write Fleet proof is inferred from aggregate counters.

Existing serialized histories, ambiguity quarantine, output-proof errors, final replica/archive or owner-route reconciliation, resource limits and recovery/traffic SLOs remain required. Fault profiles enter comparisons for every adapter; distinct authority, copy, read, receipt or executable contracts still refuse ratios.

regressions: four acknowledgement policies retain distinct guarantees
early acknowledgements, wrong targets/owners/IDs, incomplete windows and invalid clocks refuse
every cycle needs its own post-journal dispatch witness
healthy controls cannot masquerade as pauses
lost control replies, cancellation, foreign ownership and already-paused targets
both CLIs refuse invalid/missing profiles before Docker or output creation
real joined Python fault/workload threads, fsynced ledger, exact application history and independent baseline reanalysis without mutation retries
comparison retains baseline fault parameters and cross-contract refusal
validation.initial_result: The first full tooling run had one obsolete expectation that s3-outage was wholly unsupported. The capability test now reserves that assertion for still-unimplemented scenarios; new tests enforce missing/invalid store profiles before resources in both launchers. The initial failure log is retained.
validation.test_environment: Python control adapters and reference responses are fixtures, including synthetic cgroup/proof metadata for analyzer testing; they are not physical Docker, RustFS, native acknowledgement or deployment qualification.
validation.rust: No Rust source changed. Native integration/Clippy results remain separately pinned to the preceding persistence component; they were not rerun or pooled here.

toolchain: Python 3.14.6; repository format/layout commands use Rust 1.98.1
limitations: No new VM, container or cloud resource was started. The dedicated Colima profile remains stopped; unrelated profiles were not controlled.
The schedule models a bounded RustFS process freeze. Crash, packet loss, disk loss, Amazon S3 and independent failure domains remain unqualified.

Physical healthy/outage execution, ambiguous-outcome recovery drills, sustained S3 acceptance, equivalent service-contract comparisons, instrumentation overhead and repeatable latency/capacity remain open.
The code records dispatch immediately before calling the HTTP adapter, not a packet-level transmit timestamp. Witness delay is an observation, not causal attribution of the whole latency to storage.
Q1 still requires six processes/10,000 three-voter cells: 5,000 average replicas per node exceeds the unchanged 4,096 bound and the authorized five-node physical scope.
MR-13 operations/disaster fencing, MR-15 release gates and MR-16/MR-17 scale/federation remain incomplete. Earlier physical results and CI findings retain their original source pins and outcomes.
